corrections: MATERIAL, and it hits the record's central 'the margin is expanding, therefore this is pricing power, therefore the scan's compressing label is stale' claim. On the 2026-07-16 call the CFO explicitly quantified the quarter: 'Non GAAP gross margin for the quarter was 70%, an increase from 67.9% in Q2 of last year. Excluding the $36 million benefit from IEPA tariff refunds, Q2 non GAAP gross margin would have been 68.7%.' So underlying adjusted expansion is +0.8pp, not the +2.1pp the record cites. Carrying the same $36M (1.24pp of $2,892.3M revenue) through the reported line, underlying reported gross margin is ~66.6% against 66.3% a year earlier -- roughly FLAT, not the '+1.5 percentage points' the gm_trajectory and cost_curve_verified fields both assert. Management attributed the improvement to 'product cost reductions, fixed overhead leverage, and the tariff refund' -- price is not among the three. The guide raise is the same artefact: the prior 67.5-68.5% range 'reflected 100 basis points of impact from tariffs', and the raise to 68-69% follows a refund of tariffs already paid, so it is a reversal of a cost, not evidence the company can price. The record's strongest sentence -- 'a company that absorbs an input-cost shock and still expands margin is not commoditising; it is exercising price' -- is not supported by the primary disclosure, and it is the same sentence that carries the WIDE moat grade and the rejection of the scan's compressing-margin flag. THREE SMALLER FIXES. (1) Live price is stale: $400.13 at 2026-08-11 against the record's $365.33 as-of 2026-08-04 (+9.5%), so the base case sits ~23% below spot, not ~15% -- the numeric_gate G1A flag is correct and the 'attractive near $300' entry is further away, not closer. (2) The June-quarter buyback was $379M at an average of $439 per share (management's figure), not '$380M at an average near $422' -- the timing point the record makes is understated, not overstated. (3) 'Bariatric volumes down roughly 10%' is management's 'declining high single digits'. FOOTNOTE THAT CUTS THE OTHER WAY, stated for completeness: the two placement-quality metrics the bear cites both moved in the company's favour in the same quarter -- leasing was 54% of da Vinci placements versus 56% in Q1 and 49% a year earlier, and the purchased-system ASP rose to $1.6M from $1.5M. The bear's -10% ASP and rising-lease-deferral assumptions remain scenario assumptions with no evidence yet in the tape. Segment levels check out and net to nothing: verified TTM Instruments & Accessories $6.598B (record $6.6B), Systems $2.712B (record $2.6B), Services $1.724B (record $1.8B); re-running the record's own multiples gives $312 against its $313, so base_fv_px does not move and I am not manufacturing a repricing.
